question: Which fasting plasma glucose value meets the WHO diagnostic threshold for diabetes mellitus?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: 110 mg/dL defines impaired fasting glucose (pre-diabetes), not diabetes.

answers.text: ≥126 mg/dL on two occasions (or once with symptoms)

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Fasting plasma glucose ≥126 mg/dL (7.0 mmol/L) is the diagnostic threshold for diabetes.
A random glucose ≥200 mg/dL (not 140) with symptoms is diagnostic. 140 mg/dL is the 2-hour OGTT impaired glucose tolerance cut-off.
≥100 mg/dL defines impaired fasting glucose on the ADA scale; the diagnostic cut-off for diabetes is higher.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the four diagnostic criteria: FPG ≥126, 2-h OGTT ≥200, HbA1c ≥6.5%, or random glucose ≥200 mg/dL with symptoms.
Well done — fasting plasma glucose ≥126 mg/dL is a core diagnostic criterion you must memorise.
